sourceAudio.derivedBy: ffmpeg stream-copy of the MP4 AAC audio track; no transcoding
limitations: The audio stream contains speech and non-speech components mixed together; it is not a clean music stem.
The source video does not identify the music title, creator, license, ownership, or edit provenance.

reviewMethod.coverage: Five gap-free bounded audio segments cover 0.000-48.667 seconds. Each segment was decoded to 16 kHz mono PCM for actual waveform analysis; no frame, subtitle, or OCR evidence was used as proof of audio content.

eventClassifiers.name: MIT AST AudioSet
eventClassifiers.method: multi-label sigmoid classification on decoded PCM
limitations: Labels are machine proposals, not ground truth.
Speech/music mixtures can make precise sound-effect labels unstable.

eventClassifiers.name: Apple SoundAnalysis
eventClassifiers.method: built-in macOS sound classification on the complete AAC source
limitations: Top labels contain false-positive-like alternatives under dense speech/music mixtures.
Exact effect names are retained as unknown unless both time localization and classifier pattern are stable.

signalChecks.silenceDetect: ffmpeg silencedetect, threshold -50 dB, minimum duration 0.10 s
signalChecks.result: No >=0.10 s silence was found from 0.000 through 48.470635 s; a 0.208118 s silent tail was detected from 48.470635 to 48.678753 s.

segments.label: opening promise and initial result montage
observations: Speech is present throughout the bounded segment.
Background music is detected throughout all three AST windows (music probability 0.676-0.773) and is also proposed by Apple SoundAnalysis in the same opening scope.
Music is not absent in the opening; no stable, high-confidence discrete one-shot sound effect was established separately from the mixed speech/music track.
segments.musicState: present and broadly continuous under speech; exact style/title unknown
segments.soundEffectState: no distinct effect reliably established in this bounded segment; absence is not universal proof

segments.label: quality claims and simple/free transition
observations: Background music remains strongly detected in all four AST windows (music probability 0.720-0.846), so the opening music bed continues through the quality/tutorial-promise section.
Near 13-15.52 seconds Apple SoundAnalysis begins proposing plucked-string/click/typing-like transients, but their exact acoustic identity is not established from the mixed track.
segments.musicState: present and broadly continuous; no full stop detected
segments.soundEffectState: possible short transition/percussive events near the segment end; exact type unknown

segments.label: tool entry, interface and prompt input
observations: Music remains detectable at the start of the interface segment (AST music 0.684 for 15.52-19.52) but drops sharply across later windows (0.199, 0.028, 0.018, then 0.165), so the non-speech bed changes rather than remaining constant in dominance.
Both classifiers propose short typing/typewriter/click or camera-like transients around roughly 17-22 seconds; Apple typing/typewriter confidence is especially strong around 17-21 seconds.

Because the track is a speech/music/effects mixture and classifier labels disagree on exact names, the safest supported description is 'short UI/percussive typing/click-like events', not a literal keyboard action or camera shutter.
segments.musicState: present at entry but materially reduced in dominance during the interface/prompt section
segments.soundEffectState: short UI/percussive typing/click-like events detected; precise source and synchronization unknown

segments.label: loading, result reveal, adjustment and Logo transition
observations: Music is again detected in every AST window, with changing strength (0.634, 0.166, 0.632, 0.523, 0.400); it is present around the loading/result reveal but not constant in dominance.
Neither classifier establishes a unique, high-confidence result chime or export sound that can be separated from narration and music.
No >=0.10 s silence occurs in this result/adjustment segment.
segments.musicState: present through the loading/result/adjustment span with changing prominence
segments.soundEffectState: no unique result or export effect reliably established; exact transient content unknown
segments.confidence: medium-high for music presence, low for effect identity

segments.label: templates, broad claim, job-risk close and CTA
observations: Speech remains present through the spoken close.
Background music is detected in all six AST windows (0.494-0.841), becomes especially strong around 38.32-44.32 seconds, and remains detected through the CTA/end scope.

Apple SoundAnalysis also continues to propose music while intermittently proposing typing/typewriter-like transients; because the visuals are montage/CTA rather than a literal typing operation, those exact transient labels remain unknown.
No long silent outro is present: signal continues to 48.470635 seconds, followed only by a 0.208118-second silent tail.
segments.musicState: present and sustained through the broad claim and CTA; terminates only at the final ~0.2-second tail
segments.soundEffectState: no unique closing sting reliably separated; intermittent transient labels remain unidentified

crossSegmentFindings.finding: Non-speech audio is not absent: a background music bed is detected across opening, quality, result and closing scopes, with reduced dominance during the interface/prompt section.

The largest non-speech change occurs in the interface/prompt scope, where music detection drops and typing/click-like transient proposals become prominent; exact effect identity and synchronization remain unknown.
The result reveal and close retain music under narration; no dedicated result chime, export cue, or unique closing sting is established with sufficient confidence.

unknowns: Music title, performer, composer, source library, ownership, license and authorization.
Exact genre or production style beyond classifier-level 'music' proposals.
Whether short transients are baked into the music, added UI sound effects, edit accents, or environmental sounds.
Frame-accurate synchronization and intentional narrative purpose of each transient.
Whether any source audio was speed-changed, remixed or processed before publication.
